# What the replay installs, and nothing else: canfail, and the two packages it
# asks for, whose behaviour is part of every verdict it gives. didrun decides
# whether a run printed the evidence that it ran, and restore-verified puts a
# planted file back and checks it came back. canfail declares both as
# `didrun>=0.1.0` and `restore-verified>=0.1.1`, so with canfail pinned alone a
# new release of either could grade the same declaration differently under the
# same canfail version (#143).
#
# Each is pinned to the version the replay of 4 October 2026 installed (run
# 37229071997), and to the SHA-256 of both archives PyPI publishes for it. The
# "Install the replay tool" step in .github/workflows/replay.yml reads this file
# with --require-hashes, so pip refuses a package this file does not name with a
# hash, and an archive whose hash is not the one written here.
#
# To move one, change its version and both of its hashes together, from
# `curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json | jq -r '.urls[] |
# .filename + " " + .digests.sha256'`, and check the new release's own
# dependencies are still only these.
canfail==0.2.1 \
    --hash=sha256:aaca5f921a947567d4a1b11b6097097533c606a6a6011fd1cb1c1c91313be2aa \
    --hash=sha256:cabcffeb9999620c604669b1c7ebdb7efc7e2c9dace8a3c7ba02e378ebc825c6
didrun==0.1.6 \
    --hash=sha256:a507ce9e8da7e5382a9937514a52c3c6c2f98901c3f3beb180f85659098dad4d \
    --hash=sha256:bbf3b1a558174fd7563fbc154359c5efeeb406f7ce0f6b12103a8811563a2394
restore-verified==0.1.4 \
    --hash=sha256:cc51b4b84eb3118c8431be96c44fd66e069e8814d7f424b51b92905f20cd3ef7 \
    --hash=sha256:44d005f19ee33a03424158107669722603ea86a5d11e6bb96378dcedb25b8868
